name: RoboTurk
summary: RoboTurk let remote users teleoperate robots through a smartphone acting as a 6-DoF controller, with low-latency video streamed back, gathering thousands of demonstrations across tasks in a matter of days from non-expert crowds. It was the first serious attempt to treat manipulation demonstrations as a crowdsourceable resource rather than something only a lab's own operators could produce.
innovation: Phone-as-6-DoF-controller with a latency-tolerant streaming design, removing the specialized-hardware requirement.
A crowdsourcing pipeline with quality filtering for demonstration data.
matters: Established demonstration collection as a scaling problem to be engineered — the idea running through UMI, DROID and LeRobot.
limits: Largely simulation-based, and non-expert demonstrations are noisy and uneven in quality.
lineage: The earliest attempt to scale demonstration collection beyond one lab's operators.
